feedback.feedback: My manager rarely gives individual feedback. Most direction happens in group standups which makes it hard to understand how I'm personally performing or where I should be focusing my growth.

The team has been operating without a backlog for the past two sprints. We are consistently pulled into unplanned work which is making it difficult to deliver on commitments and is starting to affect morale.

Recognition on our team feels inconsistent. Some people receive public praise regularly while others doing equal or heavier work go unacknowledged. It is creating an unspoken divide that I think leadership should be aware of before it becomes a retention issue.

The onboarding process would benefit from a structured first week checklist. I had to figure out a lot of tools and processes on my own which slowed me down. A simple guide covering the key systems and who to contact for what would make a big difference for new hires.

I want to recognize how well the People team handled the recent benefits update. The communication was clear, the FAQ was helpful, and the Q&A session gave everyone a chance to ask questions. It felt like the organization genuinely cared about making sure we understood our options.

I have noticed that certain voices tend to dominate meetings and that quieter team members rarely get space to contribute. I think facilitating more structured discussion formats would help ensure everyone's perspective is heard equally.

The expense reimbursement process takes too long. Submitting a receipt and waiting three weeks for reimbursement creates unnecessary financial stress especially for employees who travel frequently. A faster approval cycle or a corporate card program would help significantly.
